encoder_method_note:
The skyline contains 16 buildings split into three clusters by tree-filled gaps, one cluster per word. Each building's height is exactly 10 times the alphabetical index of its letter (A=1 … Z=26), so heights 30, 80, 50, 30, 110 read "check", and so on; the same number is reinforced by the count of amber window stripes on each building, which equals the letter index (one stripe per floor). Reading the buildings left to right and splitting at the park gaps yields "check drawer three".

content.text:
The skyline contains 16 buildings split into three clusters by tree-filled gaps, one cluster per word. Each building's height is exactly 10 times the alphabetical index of its letter (A=1 … Z=26), so heights 30, 80, 50, 30, 110 read "check", and so on; the same number is reinforced by the count of amber window stripes on each building, which equals the letter index (one stripe per floor). Reading the buildings left to right and splitting at the park gaps yields "check drawer three".
